t: Brain-Computer Interface: EEG Sampling Desk — Simple
name: Brain-Computer Interface: EEG Sampling Desk — Simple
title: Brain-Computer Interface: EEG Sampling Desk — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] Nyquist rules: sample at twice the highest frequency. The desk computes the sampling rate per EEG band — the gamma band to 100 Hz needs 200 Hz sampling. Undersampling aliases; the desk prevents it.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Sampling for gamma to 100 Hz = 200 Hz. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.

safety: Safety: the electrodes are non-invasive here — invasive needs a clinic, always.

t: Brain-Computer Interface: Signal Detection Desk — Simple
name: Brain-Computer Interface: Signal Detection Desk — Simple
title: Brain-Computer Interface: Signal Detection Desk — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] Signals hide in noise: the desk computes the detection statistic — the SNR per trial — and the averaging needed. Averaging N trials improves SNR by √N; the trial count is computed from the target.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Trials for 3x SNR improvement = 9 trials. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
real_world_basis: SNR-averaging math is the real basis of evoked-potential BCI.

math_note: Trials for 3x SNR improvement: 9 trials [verified]; Binary entropy at p=0.5 detection: 1.0 bit [verified]

how_it_works: Divide the target SNR by the single-trial SNR, square for the trials. The demo detects three paradigms.
